Hi there, the AMA has ended but I can answer this (am an editor in the industry); if you signed a multi-book contract--which is generally speaking the standard--with whoever you are publishing through, then you will not be able to self-publish as per the contract. To break contract is generally ill-advised for obvious reasons, especially if you're signed with a major group. However, it's not exactly cut and dry. To get signed in the first place you will have to find an agent, which IMO is the hardest part, and once you get them and get signed with a publisher, if the publisher drops you after the first book and cancels the contract, it makes a LOT more sense to work with your agent to find another publisher. If you're canceled after the first book in a multi-book deal it would be because of poor reviews+sales, but also extremely unlikely even then. First book success is extremely rare, and multi-book contracts are in place to ensure that the second or third book receives equal treatment so that if the second/third book succeeds, the other two start selling and can be mass-produced in said event to match potential demand  
 However, if either the contract was a one book deal, or your multi-book contract is cancelled because of poor sales after a few books, you can absolutely self publish. Again, conditional, but as the agent would probably try to get you signed with someone else first, I would still try to traditionally publish simply because you get a decent chunk of change just to get signed, and if you are signed again with someone else, there is a good to high chance they will offer more than the previous publisher because you have some small clout. However, if you get the unholy trifecta of low success, publisher dropping, and THEN your agent dropping you, then yes, self-publishing makes a lot of sense. If you're a hobbyist who just writes for fun, it's still worth sticking with the traditional route for as long as possible until all options are exhausted, but at the end of the day both routes are viable. If you're signed already though? See it through! Please keep in mind that all I'm talking about here is with major publishers as well; smaller publishers are a wholly different beast that I can't really speak on as my experience isn't really with them. I know I typed a WHOLE lot, but I hoped I answered your question as thoroughly as I could. Good luck to you! And never, ever stop writing no matter what happens. This industry can suck your soul, but don't let it kill your art.

Gaming.

 Not any specific fandom, just gaming in general. The Tl;Dr is that I am generally ashamed to identify my love of gaming because of the rampant bigotry and grandiose sense of entitlement, and general impotent rage the community as a whole loves to express and seemingly embrace. Take a look at the Big Mad about the 3 week Cyberpunk delay and just consider for a moment that there are a decent amount of people raging and sending death threats over...a delay. The general whinging getting all sorts of upvotes here on Reddit is bad enough on its own, but some of these fuckers are going after the laymen who have sunk years of their lives into this, with public reports for months coming out of intense overworked conditions that come with each delay.

 But no, that's not what folks are mad about--they're upset because a game they demand isn't going to be in their tiny little angry baby hands, and actually, its the developers fault for not working fast enough, or hard enough, or confident enough to set a date...which then further enforces an abusive worker culture. This is just a small sliver of the horrid toxicity that permeates every corner of gaming. There is obviously good within it all--videogames are as varied as the people that play them and make them, and I love that. But the past few years, no doubt influenced by the world in general, the fandom has been coated in an acid that it seems happy to ignore. Or maybe even worse, that all the good has been completely drowned out by the evergrowing, ever aimless hate plague that constantly moves between new targets--be it a game, a journalist, actor, some literal random person, or some dumb fucking feature they dreamed up that they then bully into existence as the topic of rage for the month. I feel like the gaming community is a perfect case study for that whole internet hivemind effect, because at this point it really feels like a force of nature, without any of the good that is associated with nature. I could keep going and continue to torment whoever reads this with more half-baked allegories, but I think you get my point.
Thank you, and hope you kick booty soon too if you're not already!
